answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed raven-banding station on a named riverbank, where a licensed ringer bands wild ravens, each bird logged in a public register. Its recorder captures the dawn echo of the ravens over the river, and random checks summon the holder to replay that morning's echo live from the post within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two riverbanks at once. The permit fee in outside money doubles per further station on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another riverbank post, another ringer, another live human, and twice the prior fee.
